# spotlight_workspace_token_trust (Resource)

A CI workload whose OIDC tokens are exchanged for short-lived workspace tokens, so the CI platform stores no Spotlight token: a job whose token the trust admits calls `POST /api/workspace-tokens/exchange`, as the provider's `oidc` block does, and is given a token with the trust's scopes for its lifetime. Changing or deleting the trust stops every token it minted at once. Writing workspace token trusts needs a workspace admin, or a token granted the `trusts` scope that has every scope the trust gives. A token can give a trust only the scopes that it has. A token can change a trust only when it has the current scopes and the new scopes of the trust. Import it as `<workspace id>/<key>`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "spotlight_workspace_token_trust" "github_main" {
  workspace_id = spotlight_workspace.acme.id
  key          = "github-main"
  issuer       = "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com"
  subject      = "repo:acme/platform:ref:refs/heads/main"
  claims = {
    repository_owner = "acme"
  }
  scopes           = ["configure", "secrets"]
  lifetime_minutes = 15
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `issuer` (String) The https URL of the OIDC issuer whose signed tokens the trust accepts, as in `https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com`; its keys are found through OIDC discovery.
- `key` (String) Names the trust, and every token it mints, as in `github-main`. It is fixed for the workspace token trust's life, so changing it replaces the workspace token trust.
- `scopes` (Set of String) The scopes every token the trust mints is given: one of `read`, `plan` or `configure`, which are a ladder, and `secrets`, `runners` or `trusts` beside it, as a stored token's are. A trust that grants `trusts` lets the workloads it admits write every trust in the workspace, their own included, and so mint tokens with any scope.
- `subject` (String) The subject the workload's token must carry, as in `repo:acme/platform:ref:refs/heads/main`. `*` matches any run of characters, colons included, as in `repo:acme/platform:*`; a subject with one names its owner before the first, so `repo:acme/*` is accepted but `repo:*` and `*` are refused.
- `workspace_id` (String) The workspace the workspace token trust belongs to. Changing it replaces the workspace token trust.

### Optional

- `audience` (String) The audience the workload must ask its issuer for.
- `claims` (Map of String) Further claims the workload's token must carry, by name, each matching its pattern the way `subject` does, as in `{ repository = "acme/platform" }`.
- `lifetime_minutes` (Number) How many minutes a token the trust mints admits its bearer, from 1 to 60.

### Read-Only

- `address` (String) Names the resource within its workspace, as in `github-main`.
- `defined_by` (String) The admin who defined the trust; the tokens it mints act on their behalf.
- `id` (String) Issued by Spotlight when the workspace token trust is created, and never changed.
- `version` (Number) Rises with every change to the workspace token trust; each write sends it back so a change made since is not overwritten.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `identity` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_workspace_token_trust.github_main
  identity = {
    id = "0d6f3c1e-8a52-4f7b-9c1d-5e2a7b3f9c40"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
### Identity Schema

#### Required

- `id` (String) The id Spotlight issued the workspace token trust when it was created.

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = spotlight_workspace_token_trust.github_main
  id = "5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/github-main"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a workspace token trust with the id of its workspace and its key.
terraform import spotlight_workspace_token_trust.github_main 5b1e9d2c-7a43-4f8e-b6c0-3d9a8e1f2b57/github-main
```
